plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden flower heads that turn to follow the sun. Each head is a crowd of tiny florets, ringed by bright yellow rays. In late summer, fields glow with them and hum with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer, typically July through September in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Great Plains of the United States and temperate fields across Europe
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not one flower. It is hundreds to thousands of tiny florets, and they are arranged in spirals that follow Fibonacci numbers.

plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: Rounded clusters of papery blooms spill over glossy green leaves in cottage gardens and along shady paths. Late summer gives the blooms a faded, antique look as they age.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early summer into early autumn, typically June through September in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens in the northeastern United States, the United Kingdom and Japan
plants.funFact: Soil chemistry can change the color of its blooms. Acidic soil that makes aluminum available tends to produce blue flowers, while alkaline soil tends to produce pink.

plants.name: Eucalyptus caesia
plants.description: A weeping, silvery-stemmed tree that hangs bright pink-red blossoms from its branches. The flowers are fluffy bursts of stamens that draw nectar-feeding birds in the cool, dry months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring, with its main flowering in winter, which covers August in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Granite outcrops of southwestern Western Australia
plants.funFact: It grows wild on only a few granite outcrops in Western Australia. It is much more widely grown in gardens than it is found in the wild.
